voiceover: Did Jesus ever actually say he was God? In his book Did Jesus Really Say He Was God?, Dr. Mikel Del Rosario argues it in a surprising way — not from John's famous 'I am' sayings, but from Mark, the earliest Gospel, and the reaction of Jesus' own enemies. Scene one. Mark chapter two: a paralyzed man is lowered through a roof, and Jesus tells him his sins are forgiven. The religious scholars are stunned: 'Who can forgive sins but God alone?' Forgiving sins was God's own prerogative — and Jesus had just claimed it. Scene two. On trial for his life, the high priest asks: 'Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?' Jesus answers in the words of Daniel and the Psalms: the Son of Man, seated at the right hand of Power, coming with the clouds of heaven. The high priest tears his robes and cries blasphemy. Del Rosario's point: you don't need Jesus to say the words 'I am God.' Weigh how his enemies reacted. They understood exactly what he was claiming — divine authority. The best explanation of the earliest evidence is that he claimed it from the very start — not that the church invented his divinity later. Read the full case in Dr. Mikel Del Rosario's book, Did Jesus Really Say He Was God? — and work through it with us in our reading club.
